tagline: Twenty-seven miles of forest with no power lines in sight.
intro: Out of Snow Shoe, PA 144 runs west to Moshannon, turns north into the Sproul State Forest and becomes Ridge Road, running along the top of the plateau of the Allegheny Ridge. Hardwood forest stretches off on either hand, with evergreens and mountain laurel, and no power lines or houses come into view.

Lumber and iron companies clear-cut this land and were more than willing to sell it afterward. The first tract, bought in 1898, was the first land Pennsylvania ever bought for a state forest. Past State Camp the road winds alongside Hall Run to the West Branch Susquehanna.

moments.title: Snow Shoe
moments.text: By local tradition the borough takes its name from a pair of snowshoes found at an Indian village near the town site.

moments.title: Dennison Overlook
moments.text: Near State Camp, at about 2,200 feet and at least ten miles from any light pollution, the overlook is listed in the Dark Skies Directory and a favorite of Central Pennsylvania stargazers.

moments.title: Renovo
moments.text: The Philadelphia and Erie Railroad built the town at the halfway point of its line and named the avenues after the Great Lakes.
